questions.q: On a reaction pathway diagram, reactants are at 80 kJ, the peak at 230 kJ and products at 30 kJ. What are Ea and ΔH?
How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
options: It gives the particles more kinetic energy
It increases the concentration of the reactants
questions.why: A lower Ea means a greater proportion of collisions are successful; the catalyst is unchanged at the end.

questions.q: Marble lumps react with excess acid. The experiment is repeated with the same mass of marble powder. How does the gas-volume graph change?
options: less steep at the start; same final volume
steeper at the start; same final volume
steeper at the start; larger final volume
questions.why: Larger surface area gives a faster rate, but the same mass of limiting marble gives the same volume of gas.

questions.q: Explain, using collision theory, why increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction.
questions.model: Particles have more kinetic energy and move faster, so they collide more frequently, and a greater proportion of collisions have energy greater than or equal to the activation energy, so there are more frequent successful collisions.
points: more kinetic energy / move faster → more frequent collisions
greater proportion of particles/collisions with energy ≥ Ea (more successful collisions)
